reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) supports that boride precipitation enhances grain boundary cohesion and improves mechanical properties in a specific refractory HEA (HfMoNbTaTiZr), but none of the evidence addresses catalytic activity, selectivity, ethanol oxidation, or the PtPdRhRuIrOs system. The mechanistic link between grain boundary cohesion and catalytic performance is entirely unsupported, and E1 is irrelevant.
premises: Intergranular boride precipitation enhances grain boundary cohesion in high-entropy alloys
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion improves mechanical properties (e.g., ductility, work hardenability)
Improved grain boundary cohesion can be achieved by minor boron addition in refractory HEAs
Grain boundary cohesion affects catalytic activity and selectivity by modifying reactant/product transport
These effects observed in HfMoNbTaTiZr will translate to PtPdRhRuIrOs under ethanol oxidation conditions
